beats.text: Google often guesses your search before you finish typing. It's not reading your mind.
Those suggestions come from real searches people have already made.
It weighs what's trending, what's common where you are, and what you've searched before.
But finding the answer is the bigger trick.
Bots called crawlers visit public web pages and follow every link they find.
Everything they find goes into Google's index: hundreds of billions of pages, over a hundred million gigabytes.
It works like the index at the back of a book: Google checks the index, not the whole web, which is why it's instant.
Then hundreds of signals, like your language, location and device, decide what you see first.
So when you hit Enter, Google isn't searching the internet. It already did, and it's just checking its notes.
